interpretation_notes: What passed: all three validity controls and every N = 1 acceptance criterion this stage could judge. C2 passed as a reproduction test on seed 45, with L0-raw failing exactly the 8 predicted entries. C1: each known-defect cell failed 5 of 5. C3: 42 of 44 scored mutants were killed and M12 and M13 on H-OSW-fixed came out equivalent, as predicted. C4: 700 of 700 trials agree with the R-dev reference. A1 at N = 1: 2,000 of 2,000 trials, all 100 entries in both seeds and both settings. A2: every in-spec cell 10 of 10. A3: every stress entry 60 of 60 on every layer. A6: 300 of 300. A5 passes on the 9 receipts that exist so far.

What failed, and why it is expected: the C2 failures are the predicted L0-raw mapping gaps (non-ASCII text skipped; KP_Enter; PyAutoGUI raising on buttons 8 and 9). The C1 failures are the registered parser defects. The failures in A2 and in C3's reference runs are outside-spec cells only (H-OSW-fixed R03 and R09; H-GA R02, R04, R06 and R10), the same as in development. Three C2 entries are FLAKY under section 5, but only from stale markers in the last screenshot, which C2's rule reports and does not judge. That is consistent with L0-raw having no settle or repaint wait.

What the results license: the suite is not invalidated by C1-C4, so it can be used. The L0-fixed runtime and both Stage-1 harness adapters show no failure at N = 1 over these trials. A1's per-entry zero-failure upper bound is about 13.9% (20 repetitions) and A3's about 4.9% per stress entry per layer (60 repetitions). These are per-entry bounds, not the per-action-class bounds A4 is sized for.

What they do not license: Stage-1 GPU episodes. A1 at N* > 1 (the ladder), A4, A7 and A5's final judgement over every acceptance receipt are still pending, and A7 alone gates the screenshot-plus-accessibility setting. Zero restarts in 7,172 accessibility calls is unremarkable: the registration gives about 0.41 probability of seeing none at the development rate. It says little about A7's 5 x 10^-4 bound.

C2 is a reproduction test, not an a-priori test, and its pass depends on decisions D43 and D45. Every key event read without its state in the whole programme occurs in C2's four L0-raw shell-grabbed chords (53 events), each 0-2 ms after the grab key's processed press. Under v1's reading, chord_super_d's d press (state 0, no Mod4) would fail, as it did in v1's a-priori C2 (job 768). The registration discloses this. The judge rule was adopted after seeing v1's failure, so v2's C2 cannot count as independent evidence that L0-raw's failing set was predicted.

Conversely, the acceptance verdicts do not depend on D43 or D45. Across 355,620 key events in A1-A3, and in C1 and C3, every tap key event carried Mod2, so no event in those criteria was read without its state. They would be the same under the stricter v1 reading. chord_super_d passed all 40 of its L0-fixed-path trials with full state.

C3 repeated development's seed-42 conditions with mutants already known to be killed in development (jobs 553-602). It confirms that the frozen code and kit still detect every mutant. It is not an independent estimate of the suite's sensitivity, and the bundle reports it that way.

Process integrity holds. No campaign ran before its ledger row, nothing was rerun, there was no repair attempt (attempt 1 everywhere, no executor-aN row), and every job's end state was recorded and agrees with its batch record. Every manifest is reproducible from a byte-identical export and is admitted by manifest.py (A5 by the infrastructure-validation path). The per-trial verdicts the analysis reads are exactly what the frozen judge gives on the stored raw records.

Surprising or worth noting: other sessions' GPU reviewer jobs (16 CPUs each) and s1a-* CPU jobs ran during A5, A2 and A3. This is irrelevant at N = 1, but it matters for the ladder: section 9 aborts a rung if a foreign job starts, so a quiet host window must be arranged. Every Slurm record shows Requeue=1 (Restarts=0 so far), which matters for the long A4 and A7 jobs. HMP sendkey menu reaches X in 0 of 21 boots, as job 374 recorded. H-GA-buggy's R14 corner click lands at (1918, 1078), not (1919, 1079), and its R09 wheel turns the opposite way. Both cells are outside C1's judged set.
